correctness.rationale: Exact conditional NGN displacement follows by substituting the two positive quadratic losses into the cited formula. Cross multiplication gives x times At²+Bt+C with a strictly positive denominator, reducing the five-distinct-root question to two positive distinct quadratic roots. B<0 and Δ>0 force a nonempty exact d interval, whose threshold is A>5+4sqrt(2). At its lower endpoint C=B²/(4A)>0 by Δ=0, ensuring the existence of an interior d with C>0. Exact factorization at A=12,d=8/5 yields five roots and exact stable/unstable multipliers. Replay of standalone symbolic verifier succeeded; no stochastic path convergence is inferred.

value.rationale: The count and attractivity of zeros of NGN conditional mean drift are a natural, quantitatively meaningful obstruction to treating positive strongly convex sample losses as guaranteeing a unique averaged fixed point. A necessary-and-sufficient parameter threshold and explicit suboptimal attracting fixed-point pair are materially stronger than a generic observation of stochastic bias, and help diagnose fixed-regularization mean dynamics. It is expressly limited to conditional-mean map and does not overclaim stochastic attraction.
